analysis: The PR changes only documentation in docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The visible patch adds, near head line 584, a description of benchmark scheduler-prefill schema 5 fields (prefillChunkTokens, maxBatchedTokensPerStep, soloPrefillStripeTokens). It also documents that a measured engine built with different geometry fails the run. The second hunk, at head line 1759, adds an environment-variable table row for DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS. I examined both base units, which contain the surrounding text, for cross-references to the threat model. The benchmark section is a developer harness, runs with the prefix cache disabled, and does not touch the coordinator WebSocket, attestation, the encrypted SSD cache (T-041), App Attest authorization (TB-011), key handling or logout. The text introduces no new network, credential or storage surface, and it does not change documented security claims such as cache TTL, the default-on state or the logout semantics. The documented environment variables tune prefill chunk size and step token budget. These are performance and admission knobs. Their DoS or memory-admission effects live in code that is not part of this PR. The patch excerpt is marked incomplete, so only the visible hunks were assessed. The remaining question is whether the backing code change in EngineV2Factory, such as the new geometry validation and the new env keys, alters memory admission or the prefill limits documented elsewhere. That code is outside the supplied evidence. No finding is raised.
